info.title: freehire API
info.description:
## Base URL

All endpoints are served under `https://freehire.me/api/v1`. The API is read-first and open: the job, search, facet, and company endpoints need no authentication and may be called cross-origin.

Authenticated endpoints accept either the browser session cookie (set by sign-in, same-origin) or a personal API key sent as a Bearer token — see the authentication model below. Keys are created in your account, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys), not through this API.

## Response envelope

Single items are wrapped as `{ "data": ... }`. Collections add pagination metadata: `{ "data": [...], "meta": { "total", "limit", "offset" } }`. Errors are `{ "error": "message" }` with a matching HTTP status.

```json
{ "data": { "...": "single item" } }

{ "data": [ ... ], "meta": { "total": 4213, "limit": 20, "offset": 0 } }

{ "error": "job not found" }
```

## Pagination

List and search endpoints page with `limit` (default 20, max 100) and `offset` (default 0). `meta.total` reports the total matching the current filters, so you can compute the number of pages.

Pagination is bounded on **every** list endpoint: `offset + limit` may not exceed 10000 (`pagination too deep` → 400). This is deep-paging protection, not a cap on the reported total — use filters to narrow rather than paging that far.

The bound is a refusal rather than a clamp, deliberately: a clamped page would answer 200 carrying rows you did not ask for, and a client walking pages would loop over the same page forever without being able to tell. A 400 means "there is no such page", which is the truth.

## Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes: 400 (bad request / invalid value), 401 (missing or invalid credentials), 403 (authenticated but not allowed, e.g. a non-moderator), 404 (no such job, company, or owned resource), 429 (request limit exceeded), and 503 (service temporarily unavailable). Application errors use `{ "error": ... }`. nginx rate-limit rejections can return a non-JSON body; see API plans below.

## API plans

The public read endpoints answer without a key for personal and non-commercial use. Showing the postings in a product you offer to others needs an [API plan](https://freehire.me/jobs-api), under the [data licence](https://freehire.me/terms#data-licence).

Send a full-access key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or use the OAuth access token of a signed-in MCP or CLI connection.

The API plan allows 1,200 requests per 60-second window. The Data plan allows 6,000. Neither paid API plan has a daily request cap. The account shares one budget across its full-access API keys and OAuth connections, including public REST reads and agent search. A browser session cookie does not select the paid API rate.

The limit counts HTTP requests, not returned listings or unique vacancies. A page containing 100 listings costs one request. Re-fetching the same page or vacancy costs another request, including when the data has not changed. There is no separate cooldown for refreshing a vacancy.

Pagination returns 20 listings by default and up to 100 with `limit=100`. Requests carrying `offset` or `company_slug` also pass through separate per-IP nginx limits of 2 requests per second each, including paid requests. The `offset` limit allows a burst of 50 excess requests; the `company_slug` limit allows 30. A request carrying both parameters draws on both limits. For sustained pagination or company-filtered reads, keep the combined traffic from one IP within the applicable 2-request-per-second limit.

The gateway returns `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (seconds until reset). A window starts with its first request. Exceeding a request limit returns HTTP 429. Gateway rejections include `Retry-After` in seconds; nginx rejections can omit these headers and return a non-JSON body. Pause for `Retry-After` when present; otherwise back off before retrying.

## Authentication model

Browser clients authenticate with an `HttpOnly` session cookie set on sign-in (same-origin; the SPA cannot read it). Non-browser clients use a personal API key as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

Endpoints marked “Session or API key” accept either; endpoints marked “Session only” (saved searches, subscriptions) accept only the cookie, so a leaked key cannot manage credentials. “Moderator” endpoints additionally require the moderator role.

## What is not here

This reference covers every endpoint you can call. A handful are deliberately left out because calling them directly is meaningless: the Gmail and calendar consent redirects (`/me/gmail/connect`, `/me/calendar/connect`, and their callbacks), which only a browser can complete; the Telegram bot webhook; the browser-tool websocket relay; the sitemap-cursor helpers behind `/sitemap.xml`; and the `/og/*.png` social-preview cards, which render an image rather than answer with JSON.

Managing API keys (`POST`, `GET` and `DELETE` on `/me/api-keys`) is not documented here, because no API client can call it. Those endpoints accept only the browser session cookie, and additionally require a freshly proven identity — a password re-entry or a sign-in-provider check — that a script has no way to supply. Create and revoke keys in your account instead, at [freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys](https://freehire.me/my/integrations/api-keys); the plaintext token is shown exactly once, at creation, so store it then.

The `/jobs/{slug}/fit` endpoints are pre-rename aliases of `/jobs/{slug}/match-analysis` and hit the same handlers. They still work, so existing clients do not break — use the match-analysis paths in new code.

Most of this API is also a CLI. If you are writing an agent rather than an integration, `freehire` covers the same surface with less ceremony — search, tracking, the inbox and CV tailoring — over one API key.

## External vs internal endpoints

This reference covers every endpoint a client can call from outside the browser: public reads, and endpoints that also accept a personal API key. Endpoints that require the browser’s own session cookie — saved searches, notifications, moderator tools, the browser extension — are not reachable with a key alone and are documented separately at [freehire.me/docs/api/internal](https://freehire.me/docs/api/internal).

## Filtering jobs



Except where noted below, these parameters apply to `GET /jobs/search` and `GET /jobs/facets`. Combine any of them with full-text `q`.



- Pass multiple values as a comma-separated list to OR them: `skills=go,rust` matches either. Repeating the param (`skills=go&skills=rust`) also works.

- Add `<param>_mode=and` to require all selected values: `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and` matches both.

- Add `<param>_exclude=<value>` to exclude matches: `company_type_exclude=outstaff` drops outstaff jobs.

- Different facets are ANDed together; numeric and boolean filters are ANDed too. The geography facets are the one exception — see below.

- Geography is a single OR group: `regions`, `countries`, `metros` and `cities` widen each other instead of narrowing. `regions=eu&countries=IT` means "in Europe **or** in Italy", so it returns everything `regions=eu` alone would. To search one country, drop the region: `countries=IT`. The four name a single concept — *where* — so picking two places reads as "either", which is what makes `regions=eu&countries=BR` ("Europe or Brazil") useful. There is no AND to switch on: `_mode=and` does not apply to geography.

- Use `regions=none` to match jobs with no resolved geography (an empty region set); it ORs with real region values and supports `_exclude` like any region.

- A param no filter reads is ignored rather than refused — so old links and saved searches keep working — and comes back in `meta.ignored_params`, with `did_you_mean` when it is only the singular of a real facet. Check it: a dropped filter otherwise looks like a genuinely broad result. At most 10 are listed per response. The same report rides on `/jobs/facets`, `/market/coverage` and `/companies`, which answer `{"data": ...}` and grow a `meta` block only when there is something to warn about. `/companies` filters on its own vocabulary, so a jobs facet sent there is reported as ignored.



### Facets



Every facet below supports repeat-OR, `_mode=and`, and `_exclude` as described above.



| Param | Filter | Values |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `collections` | Collection | yc, techstars, a16z-portfolio, a16z-speedrun, sequoia, accel, greylock, usv, bond, lightspeed, index-ventures, softbank-vision-fund, founders-fund, european, ai, mag7, bigtech, unicorn, fortune500, eastern-roots, indian-roots, ai-native, uk-skilled-worker-sponsor, nl-recognised-sponsor, us-h1b-sponsor, ca-lmia-employer, ie-permit-employer, dk-fast-track-company |

| `regions` | Region | global, north_america, latam, eu, uk, mena, africa, apac, cis, none |

| `work_mode` | Work format | remote, hybrid, onsite |

| `category` | Specialization | software_engineering, backend, frontend, fullstack, mobile, devops, sre, network_engineering, it_support, data_engineering, data_science, data_analytics, ml_ai, ai_engineering, qa, security, hardware, embedded, blockchain, architecture, design, creative, engineering_design, industrial_engineering, occupational_safety, product, project_management, healthcare, skilled_trades, retail, hospitality, logistics, education, personal_services, administration, social_services, science, manufacturing, public_safety, marketing, sales, support, business_analysis, solutions_engineering, developer_relations, technical_writing, recruiting, hr, finance, legal, operations, customer_success, other. The retired value management is still accepted and answered as role_type=people_manager |

| `ai_archetype` | AI Specialization | rag_app_builder, agent_builder, cloud_ml_platform_engineer, ml_trainer_researcher, fullstack_ai_engineer, devops_infra_engineer |

| `seniority` | Seniority | intern, junior, middle, senior, lead, staff, principal, c_level |

| `role_type` | Role type | people_manager — the title names a people-management role. One value only: carrying nothing means no management marker was found, NOT that the posting is individual-contributor work, so role_type_exclude means "no marker", not "IC" |

| `skills` | Skills | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `domains` | Industry | fintech, crypto, ecommerce, gambling, gamedev, media, travel, healthcare, edtech, govtech, devtools, cybersecurity, ai, hrtech, adtech, proptech, logistics, mobility, climatetech, other |

| `company_type` | Company type | product, startup, outsource, outstaff, agency, inhouse, government |

| `countries` | Countries | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `cities` | City | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values. Recognized dictionary aliases such as München and Köln resolve to their canonical city names. |

| `metros` | Metro area | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `relocation` | Relocation | not_supported, supported, required |

| `employment_type` | Employment | full_time, part_time, contract, internship, fellowship |

| `engagement` | Contract terms | ir35_outside, ir35_inside, w2, 1099, c2c, contract_to_hire, b2b, uop, umowa_zlecenie, umowa_o_dzielo, clt, pj, tk, gph, samozanyaty, ip, freiberuflich, arbeitnehmerueberlassung, zzp, auto_entrepreneur, portage_salarial, autonomo, monotributo — employee or own business, in each market's own term (UK IR35, US W-2/1099/C2C, Polish B2B and umowy, Brazilian CLT/PJ, Russian ТК/ГПХ/самозанятость/ИП, German, Dutch, French, Spanish and Argentine freelance statuses), as the title, the description or a source's own contract-type field states it; a posting offering several carries each, one that does not say carries none. Separate from employment_type |

| `english_level` | English | none, a1, a2, b1, b2, c1, c2, native |

| `posting_language` | Job language | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `reality` | Posting reality | fresh, stale, likely-evergreen |

| `salary_currency` | Currency | USD, EUR, GBP, RUB |

| `perks` | Perks mentioned | generous_pto, four_day_week, 401k_match, parental_leave, retirement_plan, tuition_reimbursement, unlimited_pto, health_insurance, mental_health, learning_budget, home_office_stipend, sabbatical, sign_on_bonus — matched from the description; a posting without one does not mention it, which is not the same as not offering it |

| `equity` | Equity | salary_and_equity, equity_only, not_stated — not_stated means none was read, not that the job offers no equity |

| `company_slug` | Company | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `source_type` | Source type | ats, company, aggregator, social |

| `clearance_levels` | Clearance level | none, confidential, secret, top_secret, ts_sci, public_trust, interim, other. none = no detected clearance requirement (the same postings as requires_clearance=false); other = a non-US scheme (UK SC/DV, AU NV1, NATO) or a clearance stated with no level; interim is stated beside a level, not instead of one |

| `source` | Source | Open vocabulary — call /jobs/facets for live values |

| `company_size` | Company size | 1-10, 11-50, 51-200, 201-500, 501-1000, 1000+ |

| `education_level` | Education level | none, bachelor, master, phd |

| `salary_period` | Salary period | year, month, day, hour |

| `is_tech` | Technical role | tech, non_tech |



### Numeric & boolean filters



| Param | Filter | Values |

| --- | --- | --- |

| `visa_sponsorship` | Visa sponsorship | true, false |

| `requires_clearance` | Security clearance required | true, false |

| `via_recruiter` | Posting says a recruiter publishes it for a client | true — the description says so; false — every posting not marked, including recruiter posts that never say so |

| `former_employers` | Hiring again: companies you have worked at and left | true — signed in only, read from your experience bank; a name that does not resolve to exactly one company is left out. Anonymous, it is reported in meta.ignored_params. `/jobs/facets` never applies this filter, so its counts ignore it even for signed-in callers |

| `watchlist` | Your watchlist: companies you follow | true — signed in only; an empty watchlist matches nothing. Anonymous, it is reported in meta.ignored_params. Kept in a saved search, so `watchlist=true` is the alert for new postings at the companies you follow. `/jobs/facets` never applies this filter, so its counts ignore it |

| `salary_min` | Minimum salary | integer — jobs whose minimum salary is at least this (pair with salary_currency) |

| `salary_max` | Maximum salary | integer — jobs whose maximum salary is at most this (pair with salary_currency) |

| `experience_years_min` | Minimum experience | integer — jobs requiring at least this many years |

| `experience_years_max` | Maximum experience | integer — jobs requiring at most this many years, the same figure experience_years_min bounds from below. Use 0 for jobs stating no prior experience is required. Either bound excludes jobs that state no requirement at all, unless experience_include_unspecified is set |

| `experience_include_unspecified` | Include unstated experience | true — with either experience bound, also keep the jobs that state no experience requirement (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without a bound |

| `experience_only_seniority_unspecified` | Experience only without a level | true — apply either experience bound only to the jobs that carry no seniority level; a job with a level passes the bound whatever it states. With seniority and seniority_include_unspecified this reads "one of these levels, or no level and within the bound". Has no effect without a bound |

| `seniority_include_unspecified` | Include unstated seniority | true — with seniority, also keep the jobs that carry no seniority level (most of the catalogue). Has no effect without an included seniority |

| `posted_within_days` | Posted within | integer — jobs whose SOURCE states a posting date in the last N days. Some boards restate that date on every crawl, so a job open for months can satisfy a narrow bound here; open_within_days is the one that cannot be rewritten from outside |

| `open_within_days` | Open within | integer — jobs first recorded by freehire in the last N days, i.e. how long the posting has been in the catalogue regardless of the date its source states. Independent of posted_within_days; both may be set and they narrow together |

| `apply_questions_max` | Application questions | integer ≥ 0 — jobs whose application form requires at most N questions beyond name, contact details and CV (3 = the "short form" filter). Jobs with no form freehire could read are excluded: unknown is not short |

| `auto_apply_available` | Auto-apply can attempt it | true — only postings whose ATS freehire auto-apply can currently attempt to fill and submit for; a provider-eligibility signal, never a guarantee the submission succeeds |

| `work_mode_remote_anywhere` | Remote from anywhere, other modes at home | true — with `remote` and a physical work_mode both selected and a geography facet set, reads "remote anywhere, OR hybrid/onsite within the geography" instead of ANDing them. Otherwise, or with work_mode_mode=and, it changes nothing |

| `work_mode_remote_regions` | Remote arm: regions | Region values, as regions — bound the remote arm of work_mode_remote_anywhere. Read only while it is in force |

| `work_mode_remote_countries` | Remote arm: countries | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, as countries — bound the remote arm of work_mode_remote_anywhere, ORed with work_mode_remote_regions. Read only while it is in force |



### Recipes



- **Senior Go, remote, in the CIS region** — `q=go&seniority=senior&work_mode=remote&regions=cis`

- **Backend roles, freshest first, in Germany** — `category=backend&countries=DE&sort=posted_at&order=desc`

- **One country only — no region param, or it widens back out** — `countries=IT&employment_type=contract`

- **Must use both Go and Rust** — `skills=go,rust&skills_mode=and`

- **Exclude outstaff companies** — `company_type_exclude=outstaff`

- **At least $100k, with visa sponsorship** — `salary_currency=USD&salary_min=100000&visa_sponsorship=true`

- **Excluding jobs that need a security clearance** — `clearance_levels=none`

- **Jobs stating Secret or Top Secret clearance** — `clearance_levels=secret,top_secret`

- **Only jobs that need a security clearance** — `requires_clearance=true`

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description: Public, unauthenticated reads. Jobs are returned in one wire shape (addressed by `public_slug`, never an internal id) shared by the list, detail, company, and search responses. Closed postings are excluded from lists and search and served only by the detail endpoint.

tags.name: Fit
tags.description: Personalized signals computed against the caller’s profile or stored CV. All accept the session cookie or an API key. The skill-match endpoint is deterministic (no LLM); the match-analysis endpoints run the LLM chain and draw on your daily allowance. All take the same facet filter params as search where they narrow a market or candidate set.

tags.name: Companies
tags.description: Public reads. A company detail also returns a page of its open jobs.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Full-text job search with the shared filter vocabulary, facet counts, similar jobs and the reference data behind search.

tags.name: Company feedback
tags.description: Signed-in users leave a 1–5 star rating plus category and text about a company, shown under their site-wide pseudonymous persona (never a user id). Reads are public; writes are cookie-only. A reader can report a specific review, and a moderator can hide it.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Register/login set the session cookie and return the user. Logout clears it. `me` resolves the caller (cookie or API key). OAuth sign-in is a redirect flow.

tags.name: Tracking
tags.description: Per-user tracking, addressed by the job slug. Writes are idempotent. The response is the interaction record for that job.

tags.name: Assistant
tags.description: The same agent the web app and browser extension chat with, over HTTP: create a conversation, then post messages to it. All routes accept the session cookie or an API key (`autopilot` is cookie-only — see below) and act on a session you own; someone else’s session id answers `404`, same as one that never existed. Turns run one at a time per session — a message sent while one is already running queues rather than running alongside it. `preset` selects which conversation this is: `chat` (default), `profile` (the experience interviewer), `browse` (a browsing session held from the extension’s side panel), `interview` (a mock-interview rehearsal), `debrief` (after a real one) or `apply` (the conversation about one automatic application) — the last three must name the vacancy via `?job=<slug>`, an application you already hold. An application holds one `apply` conversation: asking again returns it with `200` instead of creating a second. A `tailor` session cannot be created here; it is minted by the CV tailoring bootstrap, which knows the CV and vacancy to bind it to.

tags.name: Submissions
tags.description: Any signed-in user can submit a vacancy for moderation and read their own queue. The review actions are moderator-only; approval mints a live job.

tags.name: Reports
tags.description: Any signed-in user can flag a problem with a live vacancy. Review actions are moderator-only; resolving may soft-close the reported job.

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description: Votes on jobs and companies, and ghost reports: one person states they applied to a posting and were never answered, feeding the ghost-signal evidence used elsewhere in the API (see the `reality` field on a job). Nothing here reaches a moderator and nothing here closes the job directly.

tags.name: Résumé
tags.description: Your career profile and stored CV, session-only (a browser feature, like saved searches). The profile is a singleton keyed by your session — no id in the path. The verdict and ATS report are read-only sub-resources computed from the profile and CV; résumé storage degrades to `501` when object storage is unconfigured.

tags.name: Stats
tags.description: Aggregate market intelligence, all public and all unauthenticated. Every figure is served from a precomputed rollup rather than counted live, and nothing here exposes a record-level field or a user identifier — these are counts over the catalogue, not a way to read it.

tags.name: Contributions
tags.description: Turning a URL in the wild into something freehire knows about. One intake sequence serves every surface — the website, the bot, the extension and the CLI — deliberately, so a pasted link gets the same answer everywhere.

tags.name: Community
tags.description: The lighter per-user surfaces: a vote on a job or company, the account-level notification rule (gates the saved-job apply reminder and both lifecycle nudges), and the public discussion threads. Votes and notification settings take a key; posting to a thread is browser-owned.

tags.name: Referrals
tags.description: Two sides of the same marketplace: an employee offers to refer into the company they work at (proof required, moderated), and a candidate asks one of that company's approved referrers for an intro. A candidate never sees who the referrer is, and a referrer sees the candidate's CV only through a short-lived view. Moderation of offers is moderator-gated.

tags.name: Talent Network
tags.description: A public, anonymised catalogue of candidates who opted into being found. Membership is a single toggle on `users`, distinct from `user_profiles`; a member is addressed by a minted handle, never by their account id or username. Every string a public response carries is a value a dictionary resolved, a number or a date — never text copied from a CV — so no name, employer, institution or free-text field appears anywhere in it.

tags.name: CV
tags.description: Your CVs, and the tailoring flow that reframes one toward a single vacancy. Authoring is browser-owned — create, update and delete are session-only — while reading a CV, patching it, and rendering the PDF also accept an API key, because that is the half a tailoring agent drives. Every CV is owner-scoped: an id you do not own is a 404, not a 403.

tags.name: Experience
tags.description: The durable record a CV is built from: employments, and the evidence atoms under them. Every atom carries who asserted it — you, or a model that inferred it — and only your own assertions may be written into a CV. Reading accepts an API key; editing is session-only.

tags.name: Mail
tags.description: Your job mail, and the link between a message and the application it belongs to. Mail arrives three ways: a connected Gmail account, the hosted freehire address, or a batch your own client pushed. Only the first two are classified by freehire — pushed mail is yours to triage, which is what makes that tier free. Everything here takes a full-scope API key, so a harness can drive the whole surface; the Gmail consent redirect is the one exception and stays browser-only.

get.summary: Search with full descriptions, for programmatic/agent consumers.
get.description:
Same text query and facet filters as `/jobs/search`, but each result carries the
`description` in full (verbatim from the database) instead of the truncated index
preview. Use `description_format` to choose how it is rendered.

Plus every filter in the "Filtering jobs" section.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Full-text query over `title`, `company`, `description`, and `location`. The first
words are required and trailing ones are dropped when too few postings match, so word
order can change the result. Operators: quotes require every quoted word in any order
(not a contiguous phrase); `-word` excludes; uppercase `OR` between words matches any
alternative (at most 5); `title:` at the start of an alternative matches it in the
title only, e.g. `title:"product owner" -junior OR title:produktchef`. `q_fields`
narrows the other alternatives. No exact-phrase matching. (e.g. `golang`)

parameters.name: q_fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated subset of `title,company,description,location` to restrict `q` to,
e.g. `title`. A name outside that set drops the whole parameter (reported in
`meta.ignored_params`) rather than partially applying. (e.g. `title`)

parameters.name: q_prefix
parameters.description:
`true` lets the last word of `q` match as the start of a longer word (`data eng`
finds `engineer`), for suggestions while someone is still typing. Off by default:
the last word is read as complete, which is much faster on broad queries.
(e.g. `true`)

parameters.name: description_format
parameters.description: `text` or `markdown`; anything else leaves the stored HTML.

get.summary: List your chat conversations, newest activity first.
get.description:
Tailoring conversations are not chats — each belongs to a CV — so they never appear
here.

post.summary: Start a new conversation.
post.description:
For shortlisting the current jobs list, pass search_query (the complete serialized
query; an empty string is valid) and a client-generated request_id UUID. Only chat
sessions accept this binding. Reusing the UUID with the same owner and canonical query
returns the same session; changing its query returns 409. Unknown search parameters
return 400 at creation. A condition that cannot be enforced when a search runs (for
example hide_seen without a readable history) fails that search instead, and the
assistant reports it rather than widening the search. Search-bound responses include
search_context: { query, brief }; the original query is immutable and the selection
brief is local to the conversation.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description:
Public slug of an application you hold. Required for `interview`/`debrief`/`apply`,
ignored otherwise. (e.g. `senior-go-engineer-acme-1a2b`)

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.summary: One owned conversation with its full transcript.
get.description: One owned conversation with its transcript.

content.text: Should I relocate for this role?

delete.summary: Delete an owned conversation and its transcript.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.summary: Stop the session’s running turn.
post.description:
A no-op (still `204`) when nothing is running — you cannot see whether a turn is live
before asking.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.summary: Buy a CV editing session another ceiling’s worth of turns.
post.description:
A CV editing session is bounded by a turn ceiling as well as by the daily session
allowance, and a turn past the ceiling is a `402` naming the session. This spends
another of the day’s CV editing sessions to raise it (no body), and is idempotent under
a double click — two calls in flight buy one ceiling, not two. `409` on any preset
other than a CV editing session: a chat is bounded by the daily assistant allowance,
and a day cannot be topped up. `402` when there is no session left to spend, with the
same body every refusal carries.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.summary: Mint a short-lived credential for a hands-free voice call.
post.description:
Only on an `interview` session; `409` otherwise. The audio itself never reaches this
server: take the returned `value` to `calls_url` (this deployment’s own realtime
gateway, not api.openai.com directly) to negotiate the WebRTC call. `501` when voice
mode is not configured.

post.summary: Append one completed spoken exchange to the transcript.
post.description:
Only on an `interview` session. Lets a call continued by typing carry the spoken turns
forward in context. Returns `204 No Content`.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

example.content: I led the migration to Kubernetes.

get.summary: The current user (cookie or API key).
get.description: Readable with a session or an API key, narrow scope included.

get.summary: List the enabled OAuth providers.
get.description: The names of the enabled sign-in providers.

post.summary: Request a password-reset code by email.
post.description:
Always answers `202`, whether or not the address has an account — this is deliberately
not an email-enumeration oracle.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

post.summary: Set a new password against a mailed code.
post.description:

Most active first. Facet params are repeatable and filter by array overlap (OR within a

Population-ranked prefix search over the embedded city dictionary, optionally narrowed
to one country. A blank `q` returns an empty list.

Roles ranked by open count or growth. Naming both category and seniority adds the
role's skill distribution and, for a signed-in caller, their coverage; that answer
is then private.

Scope by category or by country, but not both — the rollup behind it is
single-dimensional, so asking for both is a 400.

parameters.description: Rank by open count or growth.

get.summary: How fast a slice of the market is hiring, over time.
List jobs, newest first, with limit/offset pagination.
get.description:
Takes no filters at all — `limit` and `offset` are the whole vocabulary. Anything else
is ignored rather than refused, and listed in `meta.ignored_params`: a filter param
sent here returns the entire catalogue, which is indistinguishable from a narrow result
unless you check. Use `/jobs/search` to filter.

get.summary: Count of matching jobs per facet value (and numeric stats).
get.description:
The same `q` and filters as search, answered with the count of postings per facet value
and `stats` (min/max) for the numeric facets. `former_employers` and `watchlist` are
ignored. Narrow with `facets=`; naming `company_slug` there adds `companies_total` and
`top_companies`.

parameters.name: facets
parameters.description:
Comma-separated facet params to count instead of all of them, e.g. `skills,seniority`.
`company_slug` is counted only when named here. An unknown name is a 400, and so is
combining it with `disjunctive`, or `company_slug` with an `OR` query.

parameters.name: disjunctive
parameters.description:
`true` counts each facet under the full filter MINUS its own selection, so a selected
facet still shows its siblings' counts — what a live filter sidebar wants. Costs one
query per facet.

schema.description: A single item that read query params: `{"data": ...}`, plus `meta` when one was dropped.

get.summary: Resolve a posting URL to a catalogue slug.
get.description:
Answers `{"data": null}` when the posting cannot be identified, rather than 404 — "we
do not carry this" is a normal answer here. Used by the extension to tell whether the
page you are on is a job we already have. A miss also carries `meta.ats_board`: true
when the URL sits on an ATS board freehire knows how to crawl, so a client can tell a
posting worth adding from an arbitrary page.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: The posting's URL in the wild. (e.g. `https://boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/123`)

post.summary: Hand freehire a link: import the posting, and the board behind it.
post.description:
Five outcomes in one shape, distinguished by status: **200 found** — the catalogue
already carries the vacancy. Either the URL itself is stored (nothing is fetched or
written), or the page turned out to be a second copy of a posting we already carry
under another source, in which case the answer names the one we had; **201 tracked** —
we crawl that board already and the posting just had not landed, so it was imported
now; **201 imported** — imported, and its board queued for onboarding; **201 review** —
imported, but its careers site names no board we can crawl, so the link went to manual
triage; **202 queued** — nothing could read the page, so the link went to manual
triage. `company_slug` is returned whenever the catalogue already carries the employer,
through any source — independent of what became of the board. A URL that is not http(s)
is a 422.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

202.description: The request has been accepted for processing, but processing has not yet completed.

get.summary: Full-text + faceted search over open jobs.
get.description:
Free-text `q` plus any filter (the "Filtering jobs" section). Repeated values OR;
`<param>_mode=and` requires all, `<param>_exclude` excludes. Newest first without `q`,
by relevance with it. An unread param is listed in `meta.ignored_params`: check it, a
dropped filter looks like a broad result.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Full-text query over `title`, `company`, `description`, and `location`. The first
words are required and trailing ones are dropped when too few postings match, so word
order can change the result. Operators: quotes require every quoted word in any order
(not a contiguous phrase); `-word` excludes; uppercase `OR` between words matches any
alternative (at most 5); `title:` at the start of an alternative matches it in the
title only, e.g. `title:"product owner" -junior OR title:produktchef`. `q_fields`
narrows the other alternatives. No exact-phrase matching. (e.g. `golang`)

parameters.name: q_fields
parameters.description:
Comma-separated subset of `title,company,description,location` to restrict `q` to,
e.g. `title`. A name outside that set drops the whole parameter (reported in
`meta.ignored_params`) rather than partially applying. (e.g. `title`)

parameters.name: q_prefix
parameters.description:
`true` lets the last word of `q` match as the start of a longer word (`data eng`
finds `engineer`), for suggestions while someone is still typing. Off by default:
the last word is read as complete, which is much faster on broad queries.
(e.g. `true`)

parameters.name: hide_seen
parameters.description:
`true` leaves out the postings the signed-in caller has already opened (the 1000 most
recently viewed, saved, applied to or hidden), inside the search, so `meta.total` and
paging stay accurate. A per-person preference, not a filter: a saved search ignores
it. Without a session or API key it is not applied and is listed in
`meta.ignored_params`. (e.g. `true`)

parameters.name: hide_applied_companies
parameters.description:
`true` excludes every posting of employers represented in the newest 1,000
applications made by the signed-in caller. Employers represented only by older
applications can remain in results. Applied inside the search, so `meta.total` and
paging describe what is left. A per-person preference, not a filter: a saved search
carrying it narrows nothing. Without a session or API key, or with a value that is
not a boolean, the search runs unhidden and the param is reported in
`meta.ignored_params`. (e.g. `true`)

parameters.name: min_skill_match
parameters.description:
Keeps only postings whose skills your profile covers by at least this percent
(1–100), across the whole ranking. Applies only with `sort=match`, to a signed-in
caller with profile skills; the read stops once no later posting can qualify or at a
depth bound, and then `meta.total` is a minimum with
`meta.total_is_lower_bound: true`. A per-person preference: a saved search ignores
it. Otherwise it is not applied and is listed in `meta.ignored_params`. (e.g. `70`)

get.summary: A single job by its public slug (serves closed jobs too).
get.description:
One job by public slug. A signed-in caller also gets their own vote and auto-apply
status. A slug that no longer exists still answers with its posting when its shortcode
names exactly one.

post.summary: Mark the job as applied to.
post.description:
Send `applied_on` to record an application on the day it was actually sent — importing
a history, or correcting a date already stored. A date you state overrides one we
inferred. The day is stored at noon UTC, because you are stating a day and midnight
reads as the previous date west of Greenwich. A date in the future, older than a year,
or not a calendar date, is a 400. Without a body the application is stamped now, as
before.

get.summary: The captured ATS application form for the posting.
get.description:
The questions a candidate will have to answer, shaped for reading. Only captured for a
minority of postings (roughly a sixth of technical ATS platforms are readable at all) —
no captured form is a `404`, distinguishable from an unknown slug (also `404`, but at
the job lookup rather than the form lookup).

questions.text: Why do you want to work here?

get.summary: Other open postings in the same role cluster (per-city duplicates).
get.description:
The per-city openings folded under one canonical card by content-dedup — each keeps its
own `location` and `apply_url` so a seeker picks their city. The anchor job itself is
included. `meta.total` is the whole cluster size, so it stays accurate when the list is
a capped page.

get.summary: The application form of a vacancy that takes applications on freehire.
get.description:
Only for a posting whose `direct_apply` is true — its employer published it here and
receives applications by email. Any other posting is a `404`. Signed in with the
browser session, the response also carries `applied`, a `prefill` of your earlier
answers to the same questions, and `cvs` — the CV you tailored for this vacancy and
whether you uploaded one; an API key never sees those. `open` is false once the vacancy
closed. `501` when this deployment cannot deliver applications.

post.summary: Dismiss (swipe away) the job.
post.description:
Only keeps the job out of the swipe deck; it stays visible in the public `/jobs` list
and search. Idempotent.

delete.summary: Undismiss the job (no-op if not dismissed).

post.summary: File a claim that you applied and got no response.
post.description:
An unproven (unverified) address is a `403`; a closed job or a claim you already have
on this job is a `409`.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

delete.summary: Withdraw your claim about this job.
delete.description: A claim that is absent or already withdrawn is a `404`.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.summary: Deterministic skill match of the job against your profile (no LLM).
get.description:
How well the job’s skills are covered by your profile skills — exact, adjacent, and
missing, plus a coverage percent. A caller without a saved profile is a 404.

get.summary: The cached AI match analysis for the job (never runs the LLM).
get.description:
Returns the cached analysis, flagged `stale` when your CV or the job changed since it
was computed, or a null analysis when none is cached. `has_cv` is false when you have
no stored CV. `allowance` reports how much of today you have used against what the day
allows, and when it resets. `tailor_allowance` reports the same for CV tailoring, which
carries its own daily ceiling, so a caller deciding between the two has both figures
here.

post.summary: Run the three-stage AI match analysis and cache it.
post.description:
Runs the match prompt-chain over your stored CV and the job, caches the result, and
returns it fresh (no `allowance` on this response). Analysing a new job draws on your
daily analysis allowance; with none left it is a `402`, and recomputing an
already-analyzed job is free. `has_cv` is false when no CV is stored; a failing or
unconfigured LLM returns a null analysis (200).

post.summary: Report a problem with a job.
post.description: 404 for an unknown job, 409 for a second open report by the same person.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

delete.summary: Unsave the job (no-op if not saved).
delete.description: Unsaving a job that was never saved answers with the empty interaction.

get.description:
Searches the live Meilisearch index with the source job’s known location and
specialization as mandatory filters, ranked by keyword search on its title. Returns an
empty list when location or specialization is unknown or no visible matches remain.

patch.summary: Set the application stage and/or notes.
patch.description:
A null field is left unchanged. `stage` is a controlled vocabulary: `preparing`,
`applied`, `screening`, `responded`, `interview`, `offer`, `accepted`, `rejected`,
`withdrawn`, `expired` (an unknown value is a 400). `expired` is the outcome for an
application nobody answered; nothing sets it for you.

Vote on a job.

post.summary: Score a supplied skill list against the filtered job market.
post.description:
Stateless sibling of the CV verdict: skills come from the request body, the market from
the facet query params (same vocabulary as search; the `skills` facet is ignored as a
filter). Reports how many of the role’s vacancies your skills cover and which missing
skill unlocks the most. `400` on empty skills, `503` when search is unavailable.

patch.description:
Same as `PATCH /jobs/{slug}/track`, but addressed by the tracking-board row id instead
of the job slug — needed when a tracked application’s posting was later pruned and has
no slug left to address it by. Same `stage` vocabulary and body shape.

Clear the application stage, addressed by row id.

post.description: Records the approve or decline decision for a tailored queue entry.

get.summary: Your contact details in canonical autofill fields.
get.description:
Projected from your CV header, with the account email as a fallback — what the
extension writes into application forms.

get.summary: The boards you contributed, and their onboarding state.
List your CVs, without their documents.
get.description: The caller's TAILORED CVs, newest edit first. With a session or an API key.

get.summary: List your base CVs, without their documents.
get.description:
The non-tailored CVs you can edit, duplicate and tailor from, oldest created first.
`is_default` marks the one used when a tailor request names no base; `hand_edited`
marks a base you changed in the editor, which a new CV upload will not overwrite. GET
/me/cvs lists tailored copies and is unchanged.

post.summary: Start tailoring a CV toward one vacancy.
post.description:
Copies your base CV into a vacancy-bound tailored one and mints the short-lived
credential its agent session runs on. Requires a cached match analysis for the job (409
otherwise) and a base CV — one is seeded from your stored history when you have none,
and it is a 409 when there is nothing to seed from. Calls no LLM itself.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

get.summary: One CV with its full document.
get.description: The document without its contact block to an API key.

patch.summary: Apply a batch of edits, addressed by path.
patch.description:
An edit is a `kind` (`set`, `insert`, `remove`, `move`) and a `path` into the CV —
`summary`, `experience[2].bullets[1]`, `skills[0].items[3]`, `style.font_size`. Indices
are 0-based. The whole batch applies or none of it does: an unknown path or an index
past the end refuses the request without touching the CV. An API key edits as the
tailoring agent, so the candidate's own fields are refused and a claim about them needs
`evidence_id` from the experience bank. Every request lands in the CV's history and can
be undone on its own.

get.description: Never calls a model. With a session or an API key.

put.summary: Bind an agent session to a CV.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.summary: The match analysis a tailored CV should reframe toward.
get.description:
The split that keeps tailoring honest: `missing_have` are requirements your history
already covers but the CV buries — reframe those — and `missing_gap` are the ones it
does not, which an agent must ask about rather than invent. Served from cache; calls no
LLM. 409 when the CV is not a tailored copy or has no analysis. `job.requirements` is
what the posting itself asks for, in its own words — a fuller list than the missing_*
split, which is only what the analysis found the CV lacks. Absent when the posting
states none.

post.summary: Push a batch your own mail client fetched.
post.description:
Stored under source `external`. freehire provides no transport here and never
classifies this mail — that is the point of the tier. `external_id` (the Message-ID in
practice) is the dedup key: re-pushing the same id updates that message instead of
storing a copy, so a nightly re-sync is safe. Content columns are refreshed; your read,
deleted and triage state is not, so a re-sync cannot resurrect deleted mail or wipe a
verdict. At most 100 messages per call, applied as one transaction — an oversized batch
is refused, never truncated.

get.summary: One message in full. Marks it read.
get.description:
Use `GET /me/inbox?body=1` instead when sweeping a backlog — `read_at` means "a human
saw this", and this endpoint sets it.

post.summary: Record an application from a message, and link the message to it.
post.description:
The way out of `?link=unlinked`: mail about a job you never tracked. The application is
dated by the mail's `received_at`, not by now — the application demonstrably existed by
the time the employer wrote.

post.summary: Accept a suggested link.
post.description:
Only a deterministic match — the mail thread, or the company name in the sender or
subject — links itself. A model's pick lands here as a suggestion instead, and
`?link=suggested` is the queue of them.

post.summary: Soft-delete a message. Answers 204.
post.description:
A later re-sync will not resurrect it — deletion is reader state, not mail-server
state.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.summary: Attach a message to one of your applications.
Dismiss a suggested link without attaching it.
Undo a soft-delete. Answers 204.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.summary: Record what a message is, and optionally which application it belongs to.
post.description:
The vocabulary is closed: `acknowledgement`, `screening`, `interview_invitation`,
`assessment`, `offer`, `rejection`, `info_request`, `incomplete_application`, `other`.
Anything else is refused. A confident verdict on a linked message advances the
application's stage — strictly forward, never out of a settled stage, and a rejection
never advances anything by itself.

post.summary: Clear a message's application link; its classification stays.

get.summary: Your employments and their evidence atoms.

post.summary: Record a new achievement.
post.description:
The only route besides the assistant’s own tool that can add evidence outside a chat
session, which is why `provenance` is forced to `manual` regardless of what the body
sends — an authenticated POST with no chat transcript behind it can only honestly be
the owner’s own words. When the account has opted into requiring it, an empty `context`
is a 400.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

put.description: A keyed edit leaves the provenance alone.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

post.summary: Record a new place — a job or a project.
post.description:
An employment carries no claim of its own (only the atoms attached to it do), so
nothing about provenance applies here. `kind` is `job` or `project`; a project’s name
arrives as `name` on the wire (legacy `company` accepted as a fallback), a job’s as
`company`.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

put.description: The body is a place; blanks are kept. 404 for an id the caller does not own.

delete.summary: Remove an employment and its atoms.
delete.description: 409 for a keyed caller while the place still holds achievements.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.summary: Gmail connection status.
get.description:
`available` reflects whether the instance has Gmail OAuth configured. `status` is
`needs_reconsent` when Google revoked the grant. Connecting itself is a browser
redirect (`/me/gmail/connect`), so it is session-only and not part of the key-driven
surface.

delete.summary: Disconnect Gmail and purge the mail it synced.
delete.description:
Best-effort revokes the grant at Google, deletes the stored token, and removes the
Gmail-sourced mail. Mail from the hosted address stays.

post.summary: Start an incremental sync.
post.description:
Returns as soon as the sync is queued — a full backfill outlives the request — so poll
the inbox for results rather than reading counts here.

get.summary: List your mail, newest first, excluding deleted.
get.description:
`?body=1` returns each message's readable text inline and marks nothing read — that is
the agent read path, so sweeping a backlog never zeroes the owner's unread count
(`GET /me/emails/{id}` does mark read). Pages carrying bodies are capped at 50. An
unknown `source`, `status` or `link` value is a 400, never a silently empty page.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One classified label (see the triage vocabulary below). (e.g. `rejection`)

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: One link state: `linked`, `suggested` (awaiting your word), or `unlinked`.

parameters.name: unread
parameters.description: Only messages you have not opened.

parameters.name: unclassified
parameters.description: Only mail nothing has judged yet — the agent's work queue.

parameters.name: include_other
parameters.description:
Also list the `other` label the default hides. Asking for it by `status=other`
implies this.

parameters.name: body
parameters.description: Include each message body; caps the page at 50.

post.summary: Mark every unread message matching the filters as read.
post.description:
It takes the same filters as `GET /me/inbox` and marks exactly what that listing shows
— including the default that hides the `other` label, so an unfiltered call leaves that
mail unread. There is no undo.

parameters.name: unclassified
parameters.description: Narrow to mail nothing has judged yet.

parameters.name: include_other
parameters.description: Also mark the `other` label the default hides.

get.summary: Arranged meetings whose start falls in the date range.
get.description:
The calendar’s second layer beside `/me/timeline`: a meeting is arranged and can move
or be cancelled, unlike a ledger event which happened and cannot change. `status` is
`suggested`, `confirmed`, or `cancelled` — a cancelled meeting is still served, not
withheld. Both bounds are required, RFC3339.

get.summary: Your hosted freehire address, and whether the feature is configured.
get.description:
`address` is null until you claim one; `available` is false when the instance runs
without a mailbox domain.

post.summary: Claim your hosted address.
post.description: Registered only where a receiving domain is configured.

delete.summary: Release the address; it stops receiving.
delete.description: Drops the mailbox and its received mail; Gmail mail stays.

post.summary: Score any job text against your profile.
post.description:
The same deterministic skill coverage as `GET /jobs/{slug}/match`, but for a page that
need not be in the catalogue — this is what lets the extension show a match on any job
page. A caller with no profile is a 404. No LLM, and it draws on no allowance.

get.description: The mentor's whole schedule, weekly rows and dated overrides together.
The owner's resolved calendar for one month (`month=YYYY-MM`, default the current one).

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.
There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.description: Who is coming: the mentor's own sessions, each with the seeker's address.
The owner's own profile whatever its status; null when there is none.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

204.description: There is no content to send for this request, but the headers may be useful.

get.summary: Your plan and what it allows today.
get.description:
Which plan you are on and, for every metered AI feature, how much of today you have
used against what the day allows. Metered features need a paid plan: the free plan's
allowance is zero. The amount resets at `resets_at`; read `unlimited` per allowance, since
a paid plan can still have a finite limit for a feature such as `auto-apply`. `enforced`
says whether that ceiling turns anybody away yet — while
it is `false` a spent allowance is counted and the action still runs, so do not refuse
on `used >= limit` alone. Never runs the LLM. A pro caller also carries `pro_until` and
`pro_source` — `stripe`, `revenuecat` or `granted` — both absent on the free plan and
on a plan that has ended. `pro_source` is behavioural: a client offering an in-app
purchase must not offer one to a `stripe` subscriber, who would be charged twice for
one plan, and a `revenuecat` subscriber must be sent to their store to cancel rather
than to a web page. A tie resolves in the order `stripe`, `revenuecat`, `granted`.

get.summary: What you spent your allowances on, newest first.
get.description:
Each entry is labelled with what it bought — the job an analysis was run on, the
vacancy a CV editing session was opened for — rather than an opaque reference. A
`release` entry is one that was given back because the work produced nothing.

get.summary: Your career profile, or null if you have not saved one.
get.description: `data` is null before the first save.

The CVs you tailored for `job_slug`, or with no `job_slug` for any opening at the
company, newest first, and whether you have uploaded a CV file.

get.description: `data` is null before the first save.

Your stored survey answers. Every field is absent until you answer it.
Your current Talent Network visibility and shareable id.
get.description:
A caller who has never touched the setting reads `"off"` — the column default, not a
sentinel. `talent_handle` is absent until the first time they join: it is minted then,
and kept forever after, so leaving and rejoining never changes the URL somebody already
shared.

get.summary: What happened to your applications over a date range.
get.description:
The application-event ledger as a dated series, oldest first: applications sent,
employer replies, follow-ups and stage changes. `occurred_at` is an instant, not a day
— which day it falls on depends on your timezone, so group it client-side. `observed`
says whether the date came from a source other than you: mail-derived events carry a
date the employer set, while a stage you set yourself is dated from when you recorded
it. `email_id` and `email_subject` are present only while the message exists; deleting
it hides the content and leaves the event standing. Both bounds are required and may
span at most 366 days.

the counts always sum to `applications`. An application with `applied_at` set but no
explicit stage counts as `applied`. `reply_rate` compares your own employer-reply rate
against the rate across every candidate — both sides counted only from applications
whose owner has a connected mailbox, so a reply would have been seen. It is present
only once both your own count and the global count reach a minimum sample size; absent

callers too, and a free AI route for every account. A description that resolved nothing
is a 200 with `empty: true`.

The canonical numbers behind every "how big is this" figure on the site (the jobs list
total, the /about and /open pages). Backed by one snapshot `cmd/rollup-stats`
republishes periodically, not a live count. `exact: false` means the cache was cold and
the figures fell back to a planner estimate — treat them as approximate when it is
false.

get.summary: How much of the catalogue carries a semantic embedding, and how fast the rest is going.
get.description:
Backs the public /semantic-search page. `eligible` and `snapshot_covered` come from a
snapshot `cmd/rollup-stats` measures every few hours (the count is too slow for a
request); `queued` is the embedding queue, sampled every 15 seconds, and `covered` is
`snapshot_covered` plus how much the queue has drained since that snapshot — not
`eligible − queued`, since the queue also carries closed postings waiting to be
cleared. `rate_per_minute` counts only what left the queue over the last 10 minutes, so
a batch of new postings arriving at once does not read as negative progress. Any figure
not yet measured is `null`, never `0`.

get.description:
`viewed` is the only field here that is not a signed-in count: it is bot-filtered
job-page opens by every visitor, signed in or not, so it is orders of magnitude larger
than the rest. It is also the only one that is not all-time — `viewed_since` is the
first day it covers (null before the first rollup), because the bot-filtered counter
shipped without a backfill of the days before it. Every other field is all-time.
Aggregate-only — no user identifier is exposed.

get.description:
Served from the facet rollup rather than a live Meilisearch facet count, so a page can
show "what's inside" without paying search for it.

get.summary: Public time series of added vs. removed vacancies per period.
get.description:
Aggregated to the requested granularity over a date range; the series is dense (missing
periods are 0). Defaults: `granularity=day`, `to`=today, `from` a per-granularity
window before `to`. An unknown granularity or a range over 4000 days is a `400`.

parameters.description:
Start date (UTC). Defaults to a per-granularity window before `to`. (e.g.
`2026-01-01`)

Sanitized: which boards are healthy, cooled or failing, without error text or internal

post.summary: Submit a vacancy for review.
post.description:
A URL already awaiting review is a `409`, and so is a URL the catalogue already carries
— matched the way `/jobs/find` matches it, so a link differing only by scheme, `www.`,
tracking query or trailing slash counts as the same posting. That `409` names the
existing job (`/jobs/<public_slug>`) in its error.

201.description: The request has succeeded and a new resource has been created as a result.

post.summary: Parse a job URL into a draft submission for review before posting.
post.description:
Uses the same ATS-recognition registry as `/jobs/resolve`, but writes nothing — no job,
no submission, no allowance spent. An unrecognized URL returns an empty object rather
than an error. A URL the catalogue already carries returns only `existing_job_slug`,
and `POST /submissions` would refuse it.

get.summary: Complete what is being typed into a search box.
get.description:
Completes a PHRASE, not a word: `senior software engineer go` completes to Senior
Software Engineer at Google. Each row carries every part it names; apply them all.
Typos are forgiven in the trailing fragment only. An empty `q` returns no rows. 503 when
search is not configured.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The partly-typed query, matched against posting titles, skills, categories and companies.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: 1 to 20, default 5. A value that does not read falls back to the default.

get.summary: The public catalogue of members, filtered and paged.
get.description:
Every filter takes values from a closed vocabulary or a number; there is no free-text
search, because a card carries no free text to search. Values within one filter are OR,
different filters narrow together, and an absent filter is identical to an empty one. A
parameter this endpoint does not read — including one it recognises but cannot parse,
like `min_years=lots` — is named in `meta.ignored_params` rather than silently widening
the answer.

get.summary: How many members stand behind each filter value.
get.description:
Takes the same filters as the list and answers with the count of members behind every
value of every facet, plus the total behind the filter itself. Same shape as the
job-search facet endpoint, so one control renders either.

Each facet is counted with its OWN selection removed, while every other filter still
applies — otherwise picking one skill makes every other skill read zero and the control
silently becomes single-select.

A value nobody carries is absent rather than reported as zero. A value carried by fewer
members than the floor is offered with its number withheld: the option stays usable,
and the number does not become a way to name somebody. Counts describe the filter you
sent and never the whole membership.

handle nobody holds, and a string that could not be a handle — all answer the same 404,
so the route cannot be used to ask whether an account exists. An account’s `username`
is not an address here. Membership is re-read from the database on every request, so
leaving takes effect immediately rather than when a cache expires.
The member's photo, blurred past recognition. The original is never served.

post.description: Body is `{"text": "..."}` (max ~8000 characters, deployment-configured). The response is `text/event-stream`, not JSON: each frame is `event: <kind>` plus a `data:` line carrying the JSON event (whose own `type` field repeats the kind). Kinds: `queued` (this turn waited for one already running), `user_prompt`, `assistant_text` / `assistant_thought` (streamed deltas), `tool_use` / `tool_result`, `usage`, and exactly one terminal `result` carrying `stop_reason` (`completed`, `cancelled`, or `error`). The turn keeps running even if you stop reading — stopping it is a separate call to `.../cancel`.
